chunks: And Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The blood money (diyah) of the Jew and the Christian is four thousand dirhams, and the blood money of the Magian is eight hundred dirhams.
And he also said: Indeed, the Magian has a book called 'Jamas'.

So there is no contradiction between these narrations and the earlier ones, because the way to reconcile them is to apply them to one who is accustomed to killing the people of the covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma). If that is the case, then the Imam may obligate him the complete blood money of a Muslim on one occasion, and four thousand dirhams on another, according to what he deems most appropriate for the situation and most restraining. As for one for whom this is rare, there is no more than eight hundred dirhams upon him, according to what the earlier narrations contained, and that which indicates what we have said.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)
key_terms.جَامَاسُ: Jamas (a specific book of the Magians)
key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation for killing

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for Jews, Christians, and Magians according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani’s al-Ishtibār clarifies the jurisprudential mechanism of *ta’wil* (interpretation) to reconcile differing reports on *diyah* for *Ahl al-Kitab* and *Majusi* (Zoroastrians). It establishes that while the baseline compensation is 4,000 dirhams for Jews and Christians and 800 for Magians, the Imam may elevate the rate to the full Muslim *diyah* for those who habitually kill *dhimmis*, reflecting a principle of graduated justice based on frequency and context.
